methods.label: Recover the two totals
methods.explanation:
Multiplying an average by the number of scores gives their total. Before Payton's test was included, there were \(14\) scores, totaling \(14\cdot80=1120\). Afterward, all \(15\) scores totaled \(15\cdot81=1215\).

The only added score was Payton's, so it was
\[
1215-1120=\boxed{95},
\]
choice E.
methods.levelReason: The solution uses the elementary mean-total relationship and subtraction of a known part from a total.

candidate.annotationRationale: The assessed idea is recovering totals from arithmetic means while using the correct group sizes. Division as the inverse of multiplication supports reversing the mean calculation, and the part-total relationship identifies the added score. Weighted means and equation systems are unnecessary.
